does: Fills a hollow, a pocket or a rolled slice with a seasoned mixture, which flavours the food from inside and keeps it moist.

intro.what: Stuffing encloses a seasoned mixture in a pocket, hollow or rolled slice.
intro.why: It teaches you to leave expansion room and close seams without overpacking the wrapper.

how: Season the filling well and let it cool before it goes in.
Fill loosely. A filling swells as it cooks, and one that is packed tight bursts its wrapper.
Close the opening by folding, tying or pinning, so that the filling stays inside.
For a rolled slice, flatten the slice, spread the filling short of the edges, roll it up and tie it.
Check the centre of the filling against a trusted guide to doneness. It is the last part to heat.

cues.text: A plump, even shape with no filling showing at the seams.
It gives a little when it is pressed. It is not drum-tight.

mistakes.mistake: Packing the filling in tightly, so that the wrapper splits as it cooks.
mistakes.fix: Leave room for it to swell.

mistakes.mistake: Stuffing with a warm filling long before cooking.
mistakes.fix: Cool the filling first, and stuff just before the food goes on the heat.

quiz.question: Why should a stuffing not be packed tightly?
choices: Tight packing should stop the filling expanding at all.
Dense packing is needed to hold every kind of filling.
It needs room to swell without splitting its wrapper.
quiz.because: A filling can expand during cooking, so a little space reduces pressure against the enclosure.

quiz.question: How should filling sit on a slice that will be rolled?
choices: Spread short of the edges before rolling and tying.
Pile it beyond the edges before tying.
Leave the filling only along the outside seam.
quiz.because: Clear edges help the slice close around the filling rather than force it out.

quiz.question: Which feel suits an assembled stuffed shape?
choices: Loose with filling spilling from seams.
quiz.because: A little give indicates room in the enclosure without leaving it open.

quiz.question: The wrapper split as the filling swelled. What would you change next time?
choices: Pack the next filling more tightly.
Stretch a thinner wrapper around the same large filling.
Fill more loosely and leave expansion room.
quiz.because: Less packing pressure allows expansion without forcing the wrapper apart.
